full_judgment: 20. Every case should be considered and judged in the light of its own facts and circumstances. It is clear that in case of both the above referred decisions, it was decided to accept the house bill of lading as the evidence of shipment solely relying on the 1st part of Section 3 of the Bills of Lading Act, 1856. But, in neither of the judgments the proviso of Section 3 of the said Act was raised or discussed. A bonafide consignee or endorsee for valuable consideration can hold a bill of lading as a conclusive evidence of shipment against the Master of a vessel; but under the proviso of the said section such presumption can be rebutted or shrugged off by the Master or the person signing the said MBL by showing that there has been a misrepresentation in the bill of lading and such misrepresentation was not caused by his fault, or that it was caused by fraud of the shipper or of the holder, or some other person under whom the holder claims.
